paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: Hezekiah did the work AND he trusted the LORD to do what work could never do. He stopped up the springs, rebuilt the wall and raised the towers (2 Chronicles 32:3-5). Then he told the people, "Be strong and courageous!" and gave the reason: "there is a greater One with us than with him" (2 Chronicles 32:7). Doing your part and trusting God are not rivals, baker. They bake in the same batch.

Now look at where Hezekiah's courage came from. Sennacherib had a vast army, letters, and loud voices on the wall, and none of it changed who was with Jerusalem. Hezekiah said it plain: "With him is only the arm of flesh, but with us is the LORD our God to help us and to fight our battles" (2 Chronicles 32:8). Your troubles can be LOUD, friend, but loud is not the same as BIG. When the noise gets going, ask who is actually with you.

And when the mocking got worse, Hezekiah and the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz did not trade insults back. They "cried out to heaven in prayer," and the LORD sent an angel and saved Jerusalem (2 Chronicles 32:20-22). He gave them rest on every side. So when something bigger than you comes knocking, baker, take it to the LORD first. I know what it is to feel stuck with no way out, and I'm telling you, He hears. Hezekiah's story isn't finished yet, so keep your oven warm.
